subject.title: Add loop-aware compaction guard for saturated sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a new saturated-session compaction guard surface beyond the existing safeguard summary quality checks and post-compaction identical-tool abort, and if so what default/config/reset policy should it use?
rationale: The remaining work is not a mechanical bug fix: it changes config/default surface and decides when OpenClaw should strengthen compaction, validate summaries, and recommend reset after a degraded session.

options.title: Keep As Maintainer Design Work
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the config namespace, default behavior, validator contract, and reset-recommendation policy before accepting or replacing the config-scaffold PR.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Guard Follow-Ups
options.body: Close or split this umbrella after moving only concrete gaps into narrower issues for summary quality, post-compaction loop detection, and compaction rate limiting.

options.title: Reject New Guard Surface
options.body: Decline the new guard/config direction and rely on safeguard compaction plus the existing post-compaction loop guard and rate-limit tracker.

recommendation.title: Keep As Maintainer Design Work
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the config namespace, default behavior, validator contract, and reset-recommendation policy before accepting or replacing the config-scaffold PR.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the clearest recent owner in the current compaction and embedded-runner history and is best positioned to decide whether another core config/runtime surface belongs here.
